slides.headline: Your Confirmed Flight Can Leave Without You
slides.subheadline: Know when to negotiate—and when the airline owes you cash.

items.label: Their bet
items.body: Airlines sell beyond seat counts, expecting passengers not to show.

items.label: Your risk
items.body: Your confirmed reservation can still leave you at the gate.

visual.style: Monumental transport poster; oversized condensed typography and stark negative space.
visual.layoutTopology: Headline crown, central boarding-pass rupture, two-column footer.

slides.headline: You arrive. Your seat disappears.
slides.subheadline: When too many passengers show up, confirmed bookings outnumber seats.

items.label: Volunteers first
items.body: The airline must ask for volunteers before bumping anyone.

items.label: Not enough?
items.body: The airline then applies its boarding priorities.

visual.style: Human-scale editorial silhouette; an isolated traveler faces a closed gate.
visual.layoutTopology: Narrow left copy column; oversized right illustration; staggered item blocks.

slides.headline: Volunteer? Name your terms.
slides.subheadline: You're negotiating a deal—not claiming automatic bumping compensation.

items.label: No federal ceiling
items.body: Volunteer offers have no federal maximum.

items.label: Before accepting
items.body: Confirm your next flight, meals, hotel, transfers, voucher limits.

visual.style: Split-screen contract collage; an intact seat becomes a negotiated exchange.
visual.layoutTopology: Equal facing panels, central exchange symbol, one item beneath each panel.

slides.headline: The schedule sets the calculation
slides.subheadline: Eligible compensation uses your fare and the replacement's planned arrival.

items.label: Which schedule?
items.body: Planned arrival when arrangements are made—not your actual arrival.

items.label: Which destination?
items.body: First stopover—or final destination if there is no stopover.

visual.style: Precision timetable diagram; a frozen clock anchors a branching route.
visual.layoutTopology: Horizontal headline band; diagonal route illustration; offset explanatory captions.

slides.headline: Same disruption. Different rights.
slides.subheadline: Losing your seat doesn't always trigger denied-boarding compensation.

items.label: Canceled flight
items.body: Cancellation doesn't trigger this same compensation entitlement.

items.label: Smaller aircraft
items.body: Safety or operational swaps don't trigger this entitlement.

visual.style: High-contrast boundary map; interrupted paths distinguish separate causes.
visual.layoutTopology: Central dividing spine; two wide exception panels stacked vertically.

slides.headline: Written rights. Cash or check.
slides.subheadline: These are enforceable duties—not favors you must beg airlines to grant.

items.label: Immediate notice
items.body: If bumped involuntarily, receive written rights and boarding rules.

items.label: Eligible payment
items.body: Airlines must offer payment; you can insist on cash or check.

visual.style: Documentary evidence close-up; abstract rights notice paired with a payment slip.
visual.layoutTopology: Overlapping document hero; headline upper left; two compact margin annotations.

slides.headline: Don't surrender. Negotiate.
slides.subheadline: Identify the deal before you trade away your confirmed seat.

items.label: Protect eligibility
items.body: Meet check-in and gate deadlines. Ask why you're displaced.

items.label: Before accepting
items.body: Check fees, advance-booking rules, seat limits and blackout dates.

visual.style: Pocket field-guide graphic; bold checkmarks replace passive acceptance.
visual.layoutTopology: Oversized closing headline; two full-width checklist rails; compact publication signature.
